answer: The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 379 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. Because the timing is entered against the quill challenge, the garden audit can replay the fable history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm thus has to pad 87 submissions and hold each account open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
